items.stem: State any three merits of statutory corporations.
items.answer: Independence in operations; Freedom from government interference in finances; Flexibility; Own policies
items.markingKey: Any three of: Independence in operations; Freedom from government interference in finances; Flexibility; Own policies (1 mark each).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the merits of departmental undertakings?
items.answer: Lack of flexibility
items.markingKey: (c) "Lack of flexibility" is one of the limitations of departmental undertakings, not one of the merits of departmental undertakings.

items.stem: Distinguish between statutory corporation and government company on the basis of formation, change in objectives and powers.
items.answer: (i) Formation: statutory corporation: special Act of Parliament or State Legislature; government company: registration under the Companies Act, 2013. (ii) Change in objectives: statutory corporation: needs an amendment of the Act; government company: needs a change in its memorandum. (iii) Powers: statutory corporation: defined by its Act; government company: defined by its memorandum and articles of association.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Formation: statutory corporation: special Act of Parliament or State Legislature; government company: registration under the Companies Act, 2013. (ii) Change in objectives: statutory corporation: needs an amendment of the Act; government company: needs a change in its memorandum. (iii) Powers: statutory corporation: defined by its Act; government company: defined by its memorandum and articles of association.

items.stem: The postal service is run as part of a ministry and its staff are government employees. Identify the form of public enterprise.
items.answer: Departmental undertaking
items.markingKey: (b) Departmental undertaking. Part of a ministry; staff are government servants.

items.stem: The postal service is run as part of a ministry and its staff are government employees. Identify the form of public enterprise. Justify your answer.
items.answer: Departmental undertaking. Part of a ministry; staff are government servants.

items.stem: Identify the form of public enterprise. In each case give a reason. (ii) The Life Insurance Corporation of India was set up by a special Act of Parliament in 1956.
items.answer: (i) Government company: Government holds at least 51% of paid-up capital. (ii) Statutory corporation: Created by a special Act.

items.stem: Jain Stores Limited is owned by the Jain family and its shares are held by the public, with no government holding. (i) Identify the form of public enterprise. (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Private sector enterprise: Owned by private individuals. (ii) Any two of: owned by individuals or groups of individuals; run for profit; not owned by the government
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: owned by individuals or groups of individuals; run for profit; not owned by the government

items.stem:
The government wants to set up an enterprise for defence production that must remain under its direct control, and another for manufacturing fertilisers that should work on commercial lines with private participation.
(i) Suggest a suitable form for each. (ii) Give one reason for each choice.
items.answer: (i) Defence production: departmental undertaking. Fertilisers: government company. (ii) Departmental undertaking suits national security and direct control; a government company is easy to form, autonomous and can have private shareholders.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Defence production: departmental undertaking. Fertilisers: government company. (ii) Departmental undertaking suits national security and direct control; a government company is easy to form, autonomous and can have private shareholders.

items.stem: Which of the following is one of the merits of government companies?
items.answer: Autonomy in management
items.markingKey: (d) "Autonomy in management" is one of the merits of government companies; the others are limitations of government companies.

items.stem: An enterprise in which the Central Government holds 74% of the paid-up capital is registered under the Companies Act. (i) Identify the form of public enterprise. (ii) State two other features of it that would matter in this situation.
items.answer: (i) Government company: At least 51% held by government and registered under the Companies Act. (ii) Any two of: registered under the Companies Act, 2013; at least 51% of paid-up capital held by government; management by a board of directors; employees are not civil servants
items.markingKey: (i) identification with reason, 2 marks; (ii) any two relevant features, 1 mark each: registered under the Companies Act, 2013; at least 51% of paid-up capital held by government; management by a board of directors; employees are not civil servants

items.stem: State one difference between departmental undertaking and statutory corporation on the basis of autonomy.

items.answer: A joint venture in which a new, separate enterprise is jointly owned and managed by the partners.

items.stem: Distinguish between contractual joint venture and equity-based joint venture on the basis of ownership, control, example and new entity.
items.answer: (i) Ownership: contractual joint venture: partners do not share ownership of a new business; equity-based joint venture: partners hold equity in the new enterprise. (ii) Control: contractual joint venture: each partner keeps its own control; cooperation is by contract; equity-based joint venture: joint control by the partners through the new entity. (iii) Example: contractual joint venture: a franchise or technology agreement; equity-based joint venture: two firms forming a new company in which both hold shares. (iv) New entity: contractual joint venture: no new jointly owned entity is created; equity-based joint venture: a new jointly owned entity is created.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Ownership: contractual joint venture: partners do not share ownership of a new business; equity-based joint venture: partners hold equity in the new enterprise. (ii) Control: contractual joint venture: each partner keeps its own control; cooperation is by contract; equity-based joint venture: joint control by the partners through the new entity. (iii) Example: contractual joint venture: a franchise or technology agreement; equity-based joint venture: two firms forming a new company in which both hold shares. (iv) New entity: contractual joint venture: no new jointly owned entity is created; equity-based joint venture: a new jointly owned entity is created.

items.stem: State one difference between contractual joint venture and equity-based joint venture on the basis of new entity.
items.answer: contractual joint venture: no new jointly owned entity is created; equity-based joint venture: a new jointly owned entity is created
items.markingKey: 1 mark: contractual joint venture: no new jointly owned entity is created; equity-based joint venture: a new jointly owned entity is created

items.stem: Identify the arrangement. In each case give a reason. (i) An Indian firm and a Japanese firm form a new company in Agra in which each holds 50% of the shares. (ii) A state government and a private firm build and operate a toll highway, sharing costs and toll revenue.
items.answer: (i) Equity-based joint venture: A new jointly owned entity. (ii) Public private partnership (PPP): Government and private partner share risks and rewards in infrastructure.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each (1 identification + 1 reason): (i) Equity-based joint venture (ii) Public private partnership (PPP)

items.stem: Explain the following features of global enterprises (MNCs): (i) Huge capital resources (ii) Advanced technology.
items.answer: (i) Huge capital resources: They can raise funds from many sources and countries. (ii) Advanced technology: They use superior technology and meet international standards.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) They can raise funds from many sources and countries. (ii) They use superior technology and meet international standards.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Public sector"?
items.answer: Business organisations owned and managed by the government, wholly or partly.
items.markingKey: (a) Public sector: Business organisations owned and managed by the government, wholly or partly.
options: Business organisations owned and managed by the government, wholly or partly.
Business units owned by individuals or groups of individuals.
A company in which not less than 51% of the paid-up share capital is held by the Central Government, State Government(s), or both.
A public enterprise organised and managed as a department of a ministry, financed from and accountable to the government.

items.stem: An Indian firm and a Japanese firm form a new company in Jaipur in which each holds 50% of the shares. Identify the arrangement. Justify your answer.
items.answer: Equity-based joint venture. A new jointly owned entity.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Equity-based joint venture; 2 marks for the justification: A new jointly owned entity.

items.stem:
A global electronics company enters India through an agreement with Verma Enterprises, sets up a plant in Surat with automated machines, and runs a nationwide advertising campaign. All big decisions are taken at its head office in Seoul.
(i) Identify four features of global enterprises in this case. (ii) State one benefit to India.
items.answer: (i) Foreign collaboration; advanced technology; marketing strategies; centralised control. (ii) Employment, technology transfer, foreign investment or better products (any one).
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Foreign collaboration; advanced technology; marketing strategies; centralised control. (ii) Employment, technology transfer, foreign investment or better products (any one).

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the limitations of departmental undertakings?
items.answer: High public accountability
items.markingKey: (b) "High public accountability" is one of the merits of departmental undertakings, not one of the limitations of departmental undertakings.

items.stem: Private airlines and private banks were allowed in sectors that were earlier dominated by the government. Which policy change since 1991 is illustrated? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Reduction in industries reserved for the public sector. Sectors opened to private enterprise.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Reduction in industries reserved for the public sector; 2 marks for the justification: Sectors opened to private enterprise.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "A huge industrial organisation that operates in a number of countries through branches and subsidiaries, with centralised control from its head office."
items.answer: Global enterprise (MNC)
items.markingKey: (b) Global enterprise (MNC): A huge industrial organisation that operates in a number of countries through branches and subsidiaries, with centralised control from its head office.
